svg.text: 1. A graph. The blue nodes are chr1. The orange node, s5, is an HG002 allele that replaces s3.
2. gfa-to-tabix writes graph.segs.bed.gz, one line per node

svg.text: s5 is not on chr1, so gfa-to-tabix gives its line
the interval chr1:10-40, from the start of s2
to the end of s4, the nodes it connects to
3. gfa-to-tabix writes graph.links.bed.gz, one line per link

svg.text: A line's interval covers both its nodes, their neighbours on chr1 and any allele hanging off them, so a query anywhere
from s2 to s4 returns every link of the bubble.
4. To show chr1:12-18, a browser runs two queries

text.font-family: Menlo, Consolas, DejaVu Sans Mono, monospace

svg.text: → the lines of s2 and s5, the bars the window crosses below

text.font-family: Menlo, Consolas, DejaVu Sans Mono, monospace

svg.text: the interval Tabix searches, one bar per line of graph.segs.bed.gz
The browser keeps a link when the node file returned one of its nodes, or when both its nodes are far ends
The node file has no line for s1, s3 and s4 here, but the link lines give their positions, so the browser draws
them too (pale) and the bubble shows whole. The reference allele, s3, comes back only this way.
